questions.q:
The main function of tRNA with regards to protein synthesis is:
I. identifies amino acids and transports them to ribosomes
II. proof-reading
III. inhibits protein synthesis

In eukaryotes, in order to initiate transcription:
I. RNA strand must be present
II. RNA polymerase must be present
III. core promoter sequence must be present
questions.e: RNA polymerase needs no primer, so no RNA strand is required. It does need the enzyme and a core promoter.

questions.q:
Which one of the following statements is true regarding the DNA double helical structure?
I. The DNA double helix is coiled around a common axis known as the axis of symmetry
II. The hydrophilic deoxyribose-phosphate backbone of each chain is on the outside
III. The hydrophobic nitrogen bases are stacked inside.
questions.e: All three are standard descriptions of the Watson–Crick helix. The handwritten mark on your copy was C.

questions.q:
In the de novo synthesis of pyrimidine nucleotides:
I. the committed step is activated by ATP in prokaryotes
II. the committed step is inhibited by CTP in prokaryotes
III. the committed step is inhibited by UTP in human beings
questions.e: Prokaryote ATCase is activated by ATP and inhibited by CTP; human CPS II is inhibited by UTP.

questions.q:
In eukaryotes the enzymes involved are on the following proteins:
I. CAD protein has activities of enzymes for the de novo biosynthesis of dihydro-orotate
II. the second protein is a complex dehydrogenase located in the inner mitochondrial membrane with its active site facing the cytosol
III. the third protein has activity of only orotate phosphoribosyl transferase
questions.e: The third protein (UMP synthase) has both OPRT and OMP decarboxylase activity.

questions.q:
Consider the following about azaserine:
I. It is a structural analogue of glutamine
II. It inhibits the activity of aspartate transcarbamoylase
III. It inhibits the activity of CTP synthetase
questions.e: Azaserine mimics glutamine. PALA, not azaserine, inhibits aspartate transcarbamoylase. questions.q:
Orotic aciduria is associated with:

III. deficiency of aspartate transcarbamoylase

Consider the following:
I. HGPRT is involved in the salvage synthesis of IMP or GMP
II. deficiency of HGPRT may lead to gout
III. severe deficiency of HGPRT may lead to severe mental retardation
questions.e: HGPRT deficiency causes hyperuricaemia (gout) and, when severe, Lesch–Nyhan syndrome.

questions.q:
Retinal rod and cone cells:
I. have photoreceptor molecules which contain vitamin A
II. have photoreceptor molecules which contain a protein which is very sensitive to light
III. are cells that generate the visual nerve impulses that are propagated in the optic nerve to the brain
questions.e: Rhodopsin and the cone pigments contain retinal (vitamin A) bound to an opsin protein, and rods and cones start the visual signal. The handwritten mark on your copy was C, which would make the first statement false.

questions.q:
Retinol:
I. can be obtained directly from retinyl esters by hydrolysis
II. can be obtained from retinal by the action of alcohol dehydrogenase
III. is transported free in plasma
questions.e: Retinol travels in plasma bound to retinol-binding protein, not free.

questions.q:
The retinal cone cell:
I. has an inner segment which is metabolically very inert
II. is not the only type of excitable photo-receptor cell in the retina
III. is adapted for high light intensity vision
questions.e: The inner segment is full of mitochondria and is metabolically very active.

questions.q:
Concerning the metabolism of vitamin A:
I. intestinal mucosal cells re-esterify absorbed retinol
II. retinyl esters do not need any digestion in the gut
III. hydrolysis of retinyl esters yields retinal and activated fatty acids
questions.e: Retinyl esters are hydrolysed in the gut, and hydrolysis gives retinol plus free fatty acids, not retinal.

questions.q:
The following are involved in the metabolism of vitamin A:
I. retinol fatty-acyl coenzyme A ligase
II. chylomicrons
III. Kupffer cells in the liver
questions.e: Vitamin A is stored mainly in hepatic stellate (Ito) cells rather than Kupffer cells.

questions.q:
Special properties of retinal include the fact that:
I. the structural change on its isomerization by light is small
II. it is loosely associated with opsin
III. on its own it absorbs light maximally at 380 nm
questions.e: Retinal is bound to opsin through a Schiff base (not loosely), and free retinal absorbs maximally near 380 nm. This matches the key on your copy; the first statement is the debatable one.

questions.q:
Concerning dark adaptation:
I. in the dark only cone cells work
II. in the dark, only rod cells work
III. the number of intact photoreceptor molecules determines the sensitivity of the rods and cones
questions.e: Cones also dark-adapt (the early phase), so 'only rods work' is too strong. Sensitivity depends on the amount of intact photopigment.

questions.q:
The following is true about recovery in visual excitation:
I. the α subunit of transducin hydrolyses GTP to GDP + Pi
II. the GMP form of transducin leaves the activated phosphodiesterase
III. cytosolic hypocalcaemia inactivates guanylate cyclase
questions.e: The GDP form (not GMP) of transducin dissociates, so statement II as printed is wrong. Low cytosolic Ca²⁺ activates guanylate cyclase.

questions.q:
The following events are necessary for the generation of a visual nerve impulse:
I. establishment of a Schiff base linkage between retinal and opsin
II. decrease in the level of cyclic GMP in the rod cell
III. development of a negative potential on the inner aspect of the rod cell membrane

The ion channels in the rod and cone cells close because:
I. they are temporarily closed by calcium ions from the lamellae
II. of depletion of certain molecules associated with the gated channels
III. of depletion of cGMP from the gated channels
questions.e: Light lowers cGMP, which closes the cGMP-gated channels.

questions.q:
Recovery during visual excitation involves:
I. hydrolysis of cyclic GMP in the rod cells
II. activation of phosphodiesterase
III. activation of guanylate cyclase
questions.e: Hydrolysing cGMP and activating phosphodiesterase drive excitation. Recovery needs guanylate cyclase to make cGMP again.

questions.q:
The following support the fact that cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) is a “transmitter” in visual excitation:
I. lowered level of cyclic GMP in the cytosol after absorption of light by the rod cell
II. closure of ion channels in the rod cell membrane when the level of cyclic GMP in the cytosol is lowered
III. increased activity of phosphodiesterase after absorption of light by the rod cell

questions.e: By convention sequences are written 5′ to 3′. ATGC is not palindromic (its reverse complement is GCAT).

Translation of mRNA can begin before transcription is complete
mRNA is synthesized in the 3′ to 5′ direction
RNA polymerase binds at a promoter region upstream to the gene

questions.e: Cap and tail are eukaryote-only; coupled transcription and translation is prokaryote-only; mRNA is made 5′ to 3′; eukaryotic mRNA is spliced.

Large in size and needs to be coupled to induce an immune response
Small in size and can induce an immune response alone
Small in size and needs to be coupled to induce an immune response

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT true?
o: The term epitope is not synonymous with antigen
A viral protein may contain a large number of epitopes that are capable of interacting with many different specific antibodies
Immunologic receptors on T cells recognize continuous (linear) epitopes
Immunologic receptors on T cells recognize discontinuous (conformational) epitopes
Antibodies can recognize both continuous and discontinuous epitopes
questions.e: T cells recognise linear peptides presented on MHC, not conformational epitopes.

Penicillin can form a hapten-carrier conjugate with a self-protein that can then act as an immunogen and generate an immunoglobulin ____ antibody, and can cross-react with a number of other antibiotics.
questions.e: This is the basis of penicillin allergy.

When one antibody can bind with multiple antigens
When multiple antibodies can bind with one antigen
When multiple antibodies can bind with multiple antigens

Which of the following is chiefly found on the surface of B cells as a receptor molecule and is involved in cell activation?

questions.q:
What is the main role of chemokines?

II. Homeostatic surveillance
III. None of the above

Bacterial evasion of host defense mechanisms includes:
I. Neutralization of toxin by antibodies
II. Production of surface structures that inhibit phagocytic cells
III. Resistance to complement mediated lysis
questions.e: Toxin neutralisation by antibodies is a host defence, not bacterial evasion.

questions.q:
Interferons:
I. Prevent viral entry into cells
II. Protect against reinfections with virus
III. Play a major role in recovery from viral infections.
questions.e: Interferons induce an antiviral state that limits replication. Antibodies are what prevent entry and reinfection.

Extracellular bacteria are killed by:

Which of the following is NOT true regarding the complement system?

They can bind to bacteria, making holes in their membrane
They attract phagocytes to both foreign material and self-cells
Binding of MBLs to a bacterial capsule triggers the complement cascade
They help to eliminate immune complexes (antibody-antigen) and prevent them from damaging the body
questions.e: Complement targets foreign and damaged material; self-cells are protected by regulators.

questions.q: Which of the following key components of the complement pathway can be activated by the lectin, classical, and alternative pathways?
questions.e: All three pathways converge on C3.

When the cytokine travels through circulation and acts on a distant cell
When different cytokines have the same effects
When the cytokine acts on the same cell that produces it.
